items.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
items.summary: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life.

items.title: How to Build a Markov Chain in Python With NumPy
items.summary: A step-by-step guide to transition matrices, the Chapman–Kolmogorov equation, and stationary distributions, built around a three-state writing example. The post How to Build a Markov Chain in Python With NumPy appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: Anthropic says outdated prompting habits are slowing down Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic has made Claude Opus 5.5 the default model on all paid plans and published a guide that does away with old prompting habits. The main takeaway is to drop "think hard" and start at Medium effort.

items.title: Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy
items.summary: Cmpnd released dspy-wsp, a prototype DSPy optimizer for weight-space programming. A frontier LLM reads a small model’s weights, edits them in a sandbox, and tests each change, with no gradients and about $5 to $10 per run.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: For the first time in a while, no OpenAI model leads the MathArena AI math benchmark. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and Anthropic's Fable 5.2 have knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the top, though both cost significantly more.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei admits "there's a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year" days before a record IPO
items.summary: Days before what could be the largest IPO in history, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called buying compute 'the deepest business dilemma' his company faces. Anthropic's commitments now total nearly $901 billion, and it's still far from clear whether future revenue will justify those costs.

items.title: Meituan releases a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model that never touched an Nvidia GPU
items.summary: Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents and trained entirely on Chinese hardware. On Terminal Bench, it scores 88.4 points, landing just behind Claude Opus 5.

items.title: Bland Launches Tofu-1, a Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Model for Calls
items.summary: Bland has released Tofu-1, a full-duplex speech-to-speech model for noisy, high-stakes phone calls. It is in enterprise research preview, with no published benchmarks, size or pricing yet.

items.title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service
items.summary: Australia's central bank sees early signs that AI is hitting young entry-level workers in highly exposed jobs like software development and customer service. Since ChatGPT launched, job postings and employment among 15- to 24-year-olds in those fields have dropped more sharply than among older workers.

items.title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
items.summary: A Carnegie Mellon student’s tiny E Ink gadgets, called OATs, give houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells expressive personalities to nudge you toward better habits.

items.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
items.summary: YouTube Music and Spotify want synthetic hosts to curate your playlists. Their awkward banter and bogus song trivia are ruining the vibe.

items.title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
items.summary: The Methods Behind How LLMs Represent Token Positions

items.title: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days
items.summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on Jensen Huang's resignation and the fallout from Nvidia's leadership crisis, follow Terrence O'Brien.

items.title: Computing Effective Dimension for Quantum ML Models in PyTorch
items.summary: Local and global variants, Fisher estimation, epsilon-ball sampling, and log-space stability, with PennyLane code and a time-series experiment. The post Computing Effective Dimension for Quantum ML Models in PyTorch appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
items.summary: Megaspeed, the firm owned by ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's former lover Alice Huang, arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025, according to the WSJ. Short seller Culper Research estimates Nvidia's actual China revenue share exceeds 20 percent, far above the officially reported 7 percent.

items.title: A Practitioner's Guide to 6 Agentic GraphRAG Patterns
items.summary: How autonomous agents turn static knowledge graphs into living Context Graphs that remember decisions, user intent, and operational history The post A Practitioner's Guide to 6 Agentic GraphRAG Patterns appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images the way other AI models do. Instead of computing pixels, the language model writes Python code that places hundreds of thousands of simulated brushstrokes on a virtual canvas, complete with bristle texture and paint application.

items.title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
items.summary: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.

items.title: Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama
items.summary: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning.

items.title: Our new blog for science
items.summary: The OpenAI science blog shares new findings, practical methods, and firsthand accounts from researchers using AI to advance scientific discovery.

items.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
items.summary: Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.

items.title: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch £1m partnership
items.summary: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch a £1m partnership to help up to 25,000 young people across the UK build practical AI skills for work.

items.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
items.summary: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical […]

items.title: LVMH’s Media Division announces strategic partnership with OpenAI
items.summary: LVMH’s Media Division and OpenAI announce a partnership to support journalism with AI and make its publications more accessible through ChatGPT.

items.title: Hark Releases Handoff², a 2x Faster Computer-Use Agent for Hark Pro
items.summary: Hark has released Handoff², the computer-use agent inside Hark Pro. It averages 2x faster than v1, completes 82% of 478 internal web tasks, and learned to batch actions through latency-penalized RL.

items.title: Alibaba Releases Qwen4-Max: 2.4T MoE, 71B Active, 1M Context
items.summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a proprietary 2.4T-parameter MoE model with 71B active parameters, native vision and a 1M-token context. It costs $1.5/M input tokens and cuts Work360 cost per task by 62%.

items.title: 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?
items.summary: This article is brought to you by VicOne . VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem.

items.title: Meet Meta’s JiTTests: LLM-Generated Tests Designed to Fail Before Risky Code Lands
items.summary: Meta has moved Catching JiTTests into production. The LLM system writes tests designed to fail on risky diffs, and caught 74 privacy SEVs before landing in H1 2026, with a 60% engineer-reported true-positive rate.

items.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
items.summary: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.

items.summary: Five setups, one blind grading pack: textbook scores ran 12 to 20 of 20, but a paper published this year dropped them to 0 to 9 of 15. The post Local LLMs Handle Textbook RAG but Fail on New Research Papers appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.summary: For years, Jensen Huang has had an almost unprecedented power to shape AI's advancement as Nvidia's CEO, cofounder, and president. As The Verge wrote last week, Nvidia's chips are "the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built."
